      <description><p>Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda</p><p>Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.</p><p>The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’</p></li><li><p>Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record</p></li></ul><p>Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/13/f1-returns-to-africa-for-first-time-since-1993-with-10-year-rwanda-deal-from-early-2030s">set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s</a>. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.</p><p>Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 14:10:49 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Presidential runoff under way in Brazil</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/presidential-runoff-under-way-in-brazil</link><description>
Brazil is also heading to the polls today for a run-off vote that will decide who leads the country. The race is on a knife edge between incumbent left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio scored a major upset in the first round earlier this month, taking the lead in the vote. The campaign has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic difficulties and allegations of US interference, which Washington has denied. France 24 correspondent Jan Onoszko reports the latest from Rio de Janeiro.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8da640e8-d07a-11f1-9394-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261025-140536-140901-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8da640e8-d07a-11f1-9394-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261025-140536-140901-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">93359d74-d07a-11f1-9a02-83411c56a6a1</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 13:52:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Le Pen leads polls with up to 38% six months before election</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/le-pen-leads-polls-with-up-to-38-six-months-before-election</link><description>
The day after the first day of the National Rally congress in Orléans, in central France, passed without any major incidents, Marine Le Pen is due to deliver her first major campaign speech on Sunday afternoon, 25 October, under heavy police surveillance. The speech, centred on the theme of renewal, aims to inject a dose of optimism six months ahead of the presidential election, the candidate has reportedly said in private.
 
Gilles Ivaldi, a political science researcher at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the University of Nice, explains that the violence following protests across France in recent weeks could help the National Rally present itself as the party capable of restoring public safety and national security.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d60c29ce-d07a-11f1-9881-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26297524255923.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d60c29ce-d07a-11f1-9881-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26297524255923.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">73ca095c-d07a-11f1-ba4c-f3ad5062cd50</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 13:51:14 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France: Le Pen launches presidential campaign in Orleans</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france-le-pen-launches-presidential-campaign-in-orleans</link><description>
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen is launching her presidential campaign today. The National Rally candidate is due to deliver her first campaign speech in Orléans, addressing around 10,000 party members. Police were controlling traffic entering the city this morning, following a large anti-far-right demonstration on Saturday, where thousands of protesters marched chanting anti-fascist slogans.

On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet.

The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan, the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione.

When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen. When it reappeared on the west side again, Cassini realized that Iapetus must be darker on one side than the other, which made it harder to see when the dark side was facing Earth.

More than 300 years later, NASA sent a spacecraft named Cassini to Saturn, and that Cassini took some pretty awesome photos of Iapetus. Realizing Iapetus kind of resembled a yin-yang, it has since been nicknamed the "yin-yang moon."

How it mattered

The discovery of Iapetus, with its yin-yang bright and dark hemispheres, has added to our understanding of how moons form.

"Using the computer simulations, the researchers concluded ... the inner moons of Saturn and its gorgeous rings are all relatively young. The more distant moons Titan and Iapetus would not have been formed at the same time."

"Our best guess is that Saturn had a similar collection of moons before, but their orbits were disturbed by a special kind of orbital resonance involving Saturn's motion around the sun. Eventually, the orbits of neighboring moons crossed, and these objects collided. From this rubble, the present set of moons and rings formed."

Here's everything you need to know about the "Hunter's Moon," including where to see it, how it got its name and other tricks of the light and mind that could conspire to create a truly spectacular lunar light show.

October's moon reaches 100% illumination at 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412 GMT) on Oct. 26, as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. The shadowy terminator that separates the day and night side of the moon is conspicuously absent around this time, as are the shadows that throw craters into spectacular relief during the waxing and waning lunar phases.

Instead, it's a perfect time to explore the dark lunar "seas" that cover the moon's surface where lava flooded impact basins billions of years ago, before hardening to create enormous basaltic plains. Streaks of reflective material can also be spotted streaking away from bright young craters, where material from the lunar subsurface was excavated and cast across the moon's surface during brutal asteroid impacts.

Where and when to see the October full moon.

Stargazers in the U.S. will get their first view of the full moon as it climbs into the eastern sky at sunset on Oct. 25. Be sure to check out Time and Date's moonrise tracker to discover the exact timings for your location.

The moon often appears particularly large while close to the horizon, thanks to a phenomenon called the "Moon Effect," wherein our brains trick us into thinking that the lunar disk is larger while in close visual proximity to the ground than it is when overhead.

The moon can also take on a spectacular yellow-orange color in the hour after moonrise, as blue wavelengths of its reflected light — the shortest in the visible spectrum — are scattered during its oblique passage through Earth's atmosphere.

Why is the October full moon called the "Hunter's Moon"?

October's full moon is commonly known as the Hunter's Moon in the Northern Hemisphere because it rises soon after farmers have cleared away the summer's harvest, leaving the fields bare for hunters to catch their prey and prepare it as food for the winter, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac.

It's also called the "Migrating Moon" by the North American Cree people, in reference to the birds that travel to warmer climates around the time of its rising. The Ojibwe and the Haida know it asthe "Freezing Moon," to reflect the drop in temperature that occurs in autumn.

To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies.

Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects.

Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites.

The Pleiades open star cluster

Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore. Ancient Celtic druids would hold the celebration of Samhain — the precursor to Halloween — when the star cluster reached its highest point in the autumn night sky at midnight.

The veil separating the worlds of the living and the dead was believed to be at its thinnest around this time, granting the departed a brief window to visit the living before the realms separated once again.

The Pleiades appears as a tight collection of six or seven bright twinkling stars to the naked eye, while a pair of binoculars will reveal dozens more of the 1,000-strong star cluster.

Stargazers in the U.S. can find the Pleiades using the three familiar stars of Orion's Belt, which glisten in the eastern sky in the hours preceding midnight. Trace an imaginary line upward through the trio of stars until you find the bright orange star Aldebaran, which represents an eye of the great bull represented in the constellation Taurus. The Pleiades can be found glowing less than 15 degrees above! (Reminder: Your clenched fist held at arm's length covers about 10 degrees of sky.)

The 'Demon Star' Algol

Next we turn our gaze to the "Demon Star" Algol — a beautiful binary system that represents an eye of the monstrous Gorgon Medusa, whose severed head is depicted in the constellation Perseus.

The demonic eye appears to "wink" at us every 2.867 days, as one of a pair of co-orbiting stars eclipses the other, making Algol appear 3.3 times dimmer than usual at the climax, or "minima," of each 10-hour eclipse. Algol won't be eclipsed on Halloween night in 2026, though you may notice its light dim during the surrounding minima on Oct. 29 and Nov. 1, according to Sky and Telescope.

Cetus, the sea monster

The night sky is often described as a sea of stars, so it's only fitting that a monster lurks within its depths. The constellation Cetus — also known as the sea monster, or the whale — can be found shining in the southeastern sky after sunset in late October, with the circlet of stars representing the monster's head glistening to the right of the Pleiades for viewers in the U.S.

In Greek mythology, Cetus was a mighty sea beast that terrorized the coast of Aethiopia under the command of the god Poseidon, according to the website for NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory. The sea beast was eventually killed by the hero Perseus, who in some tellings used the severed head of medusa to turn Cetus to stone!

Spiderwebs on the moon

Look to the lunar disk in the week surrounding the full moon on Oct. 26 and you may notice a bright network of spiderweb-like patterns surrounding the Tycho, Copernicus and Kepler craters.

Thankfully, these aren't the nests of some colossal moon-dwelling arachnids, but streaks of bright material cast across the lunar surface by the violent impacts that created the bright young craters. They're best viewed around the full moon phase, when the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky.

Halloween fireballs

Our last pick is going to take a great deal of patience, and a good amount of luck! Look out for bright, slow-moving meteors belonging to the Taurid meteor shower, which appear to streak away from a patch of sky close to the Pleiades in the constellation Taurus (hence the name).

The Taurids are comprised of two separate meteor showers — the Northern Taurids and Southern Taurids — which are active in late October as Earth passes through the debris trails left by the 3-mile-wide (4.8 kilometers) Comet 2P/Encke.

Taurids are known for producing bright "fireball" meteors, which are often called "Halloween fireballs" because they tend to coincide with the annual celebration. They're spectacular and can appear anytime after the constellation Taurus rises above the horizon, which is shortly after sunset in October for stargazers in the U.S.. But they're also very rare, so it's best to treat the fireballs as a bonus if you're lucky enough to spot one, rather than a target to plan your nights around, at least outside of the shower's peaks in early November.

SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast.

The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California).

The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes.

The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. As the mission clock passed 8 minutes, B1063 began its landing burn, and it touched down about 20 seconds later on SpaceX's droneship "Of Course I Still Love You." This was the 36th launch and landing for B1063, which notably launched NASA's DART asteroid-smashing mission in November 2021.

The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn. Following that burn's execution, deployment of the vehicle's 27 satellites into LEO is scheduled to begin 62 minutes after launch.

Today's Starlink liftoff adds to SpaceX's growing constellation of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. But Starlinks aren't launching quite as often as they used to, as SpaceX shifts its focus from the Falcon 9 to its bigger and more powerful Starship rocket.

Starship is designed for full reusability and is equipped with a payload bay outfitted to accommodate SpaceX's upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites, which are too large for the workhorse Falcon 9. Starship is still under development, but once the rocket begins operational flights (and that day is getting closer), SpaceX plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant almost entirely.

Falcon 9's 100th launch of 2026 was the Starlink 10-49 group from SpaceX's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, which was later revealed to be the final Falcon 9 Starlink mission that would fly from Florida's Space Coast. The same might soon be true for Starlink launches from the West Coast as well.

The reduction in missions lifting off from Florida has slowed Falcon 9's Starlink launch cadence considerably. At their peak, these missions were flying every two to three days. But the most recent one before today lifted off 11 days ago, and that launch itself was the first Starlink mission in more than three weeks.

Today's launch was the 116th Falcon 9 flight so far in 2026, with about three-quarters of those being dedicated to Starlink. The reduced cadence will likely solidify 2025 as the Falcon 9's busiest year ever, with 165 launches completed. At its current rate, the Falcon 9 is expected to fly just under 150 missions by the end of this year.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission ]]>

On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station.

The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts.

Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station, they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node.

After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module. This made room for Harmony to then dock at its permanent home next to the Destiny module.

Why it mattered

In 2007, the International Space Station was much smaller than it is today in terms of living space for its astronaut crew. The Harmony connecting module changed all that.

The STS-120 mission opened a new phase of ISS expansion by adding a vital connecting hub for future modules. Prior to Harmony's launch, the last new room addition to the ISS had occurred in 2001, when Russia's Pirs docking module (since discarded) arrived.

The Harmony module (its original name was Node 2), was the second NASA-led hub module (after the Unity, or Node 1, module) for the ISS. It was built for NASA by the Italy-based Thales Alenia Space and is covered with five "common berthing mechanisms," or connecting points for different ISS modules.

After the two-week STS-120 flight, Harmony was moved from a temporary berth at the Unity module to the forward port on the NASA's main Destiny laboratory. Once there, it served as a connection point for Europe's Columbus lab on the starboard side, and Japan's massive Kibo lab on the port side. Some of its ports have been used by visiting caargo ships and a docking port on its roof allows visiting vehicles to park there.

Inside the module are eight payload racks that include four used for avionics and four others for either stowage or crew quarters. NASA's astronaut crew quarters are based in the Harmony module. The name Harmony was selected durng a public naming contest by NASA.

Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity.

Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth, but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky.

McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21. Each of the shooting stars can be seen racing away from the shower's apparent point of origin — or radiant — which is located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion.

Successfully imaging a shooting star takes a combination of skill, luck and patience. McCollum photographed the meteors over the course of multiple 30-second exposures taken with a Canon EOS Ra camera and RF 28-70 f2.0 lens, which was fixed unerringly on the radiant with the aid of a star tracker. The individual exposures were then combined into a single composite image using the astrophoto software PixInsight.

Canon EOS R7 camera

The Canon EOS R7 is the best camera for beginners. Despite its crop sensor, the EOS R7 can rival most full-frame cameras. It features a 34.4MP sensor, ISO range up to 32,000 and a video capability of 4K UHD 60p. It has the best tools to help a beginner master photography. Read our full Canon EOS R7 review.

The familiar stars of Orion's Belt glisten to the right of McCollum's image, close to the glow of the Orion Nebula — one of the nearest major star forming regions to Earth. The Rosette Nebula (Caldwell 49) can also be spotted embedded in the dense starfield and dust lanes of the Milky Way's galactic plane, which runs diagonally through the composite image, as can numerous star clusters.

The Orionid meteor shower is active until Nov. 7, so be sure to head outside over the next few nights for a chance to spot one of Comet 1P/Halley's dazzling shooting stars. If you're lucky, you may even spot a Halloween Fireball belonging to the Taurid meteor shower, as Earth passes through the debris streams cast off by Comet 2P/Encke!

   <description>Od víkendu si sice užijeme o hodinu spánku navíc, střídání času ale v Evropě dál budí emoce.       <description>Terčem surového útoku se stala řidička, která v omezení na dálnici D6 dodržovala rychlost. Jiný řidič ji kvůli tomu vybrzdil a brutálně napadl. <description>Běžné komerční aerolinky postupně do své flotily nasazují internetové připojení Starlink od americké společnosti SpaceX Elona Muska. Vysokorychlostní satelitní internet se začíná objevovat i na evropských spojích. Lupa otestovala Starlink během letu z Prahy do Rigy v letadle loty&#353;ského přepravce airBaltic, který v tomto ohledu patří k průkopníkům a který přislíbil takto vybavit v&#353;echna svá letadla (pokud přežije současnou finanční krizi a vysoké zadlužení).</description>

Doma, v sociálních službách i v terénu. Právě proto vznikla Cena laskavosti, kterou chce Liberecký kraj a Regionální dobrovolnické centrum poděkovat lidem, jimž není lhostejné jejich okolí. Nominace může podávat i veřejnost.</description></item><item><title>Provoz na rušné železniční trati zkomplikovala krádež kabelů zabezpečení</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904016-provoz-na-rusne-zeleznicni-trati-zkomplikovala-kradez-kabelu-zabezpeceni.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904016-provoz-na-rusne-zeleznicni-trati-zkomplikovala-kradez-kabelu-zabezpeceni.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 13:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Zhruba půlhodinové zpoždění nabírají vlaky na trati z Liberce do Raspenavy. Důvodem je krádež kabelů, které napájejí zabezpečovací zařízení a signalizaci na přejezdech. Případem už se zabývá policie.</description></item><item><title>První triatlon byl z hecu, o rok později liberecký policista zazářil na závodech Ironman</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903932-prvni-triatlon-byl-z-hecu-o-rok-pozdeji-liberecky-policista-valel-na-zavodech-ironman.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903932-prvni-triatlon-byl-z-hecu-o-rok-pozdeji-liberecky-policista-valel-na-zavodech-ironman.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 12:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Policista Josef Havelka slouží u Policie ČR přes 20 let. Plavání, cyklistice a běhu se věnoval už od dětství, ale na ostrý triatlon si z hecu troufl teprve loni a letos dokonce v Hradci Králové pokořil trať náročného závodu Ironman.</description></item><item><title>Soud se v lednu začne zabývat kauzou pádu lanovky. Od neštěstí uplynulo už pět let</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904000-soud-se-v-lednu-zacne-zabyvat-kauzou-padu-lanovky-od-nestesti-uplynulo-uz-pet-let.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/904000-soud-se-v-lednu-zacne-zabyvat-kauzou-padu-lanovky-od-nestesti-uplynulo-uz-pet-let.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:05:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Po přetržení tažného lana se ze třicetimetrové výšky zřítila kabina lanovky na Ještěd. Při nehodě zemřel průvodčí, který byl v době neštěstí sám. Od tragédie uplynulo pět let a teď konečně míří před soud. Jednání začne 20. ledna 2027. Obžalovaní jsou tři lidé a společnost České dráhy.</description></item><item><title>Viktorka statečně bojuje s těžkým onemocněním. Každý krůček doprovází velká radost</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903931-viktorka-statecne-bojuje-s-tezkym-onemocnenim-kazdy-krucek-doprovazi-velka-radost.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903931-viktorka-statecne-bojuje-s-tezkym-onemocnenim-kazdy-krucek-doprovazi-velka-radost.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 25 Oct 2026 07:02:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Viktorka se narodila jako zdravá holčička. Vyhlašuje soutěže za téměř 196 milionů korun</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903910-kraj-chysta-ctyri-opravy-silnic-a-mostu-vyhlasuje-souteze-za-temer-196-milionu-korun.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903910-kraj-chysta-ctyri-opravy-silnic-a-mostu-vyhlasuje-souteze-za-temer-196-milionu-korun.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 20:02:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Richard Beneš</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Výběrová řízení na rekonstrukce silnic v Bradlecké Lhotě, mezi Kamenickým Šenovem a Slunečnou a v Rousínově zahajuje Liberecký kraj. Chystá také náhradu mostu přes Olešku v Košťálově. Jde o čtyři zakázky dohromady s cenou téměř 196 milionů korun včetně DPH.</description></item><item><title>Velkoformátovou skleněnou mozaiku Šelmárium vytvořili v Zoo Liberec žáci uměleckých oborů</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903906-velkoformatovou-sklenenou-mozaiku-selmarium-vytvorili-v-zoo-liberec-zaci-umeleckych-oboru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903906-velkoformatovou-sklenenou-mozaiku-selmarium-vytvorili-v-zoo-liberec-zaci-umeleckych-oboru.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 17:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Richard Beneš</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Zoo Liberec představila novou velkoformátovou skleněnou mozaiku Šelmárium. Studenti na díle pracovali stovky hodin.</description></item><item><title>Pozor na německý zákaz jízdy nákladních vozidel v sobotu 31. října na všech silnicích</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903890-pozor-na-nemecky-zakaz-jizdy-nakladnich-vozidel-v-sobotu-31-rijna-na-vsech-silnicich.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903890-pozor-na-nemecky-zakaz-jizdy-nakladnich-vozidel-v-sobotu-31-rijna-na-vsech-silnicich.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 15:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Richard Beneš</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Saská policie upozorňuje, že v sobotu 31. října od 00:00 do 22:00 hod. platí v Sasku (zemské okresy Bautzen a Görlitz) a v některých dalších německých spolkových zemích zákaz jízdy nákladních vozidel tak, jak tomu standardně bývá o nedělích a ve svátcích.</description></item><item><title>Ruce pryč od médií, skandovali lidé v Liberci. Přišli bránit nezávislost ČT a rozhlasu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903966-ruce-pryc-od-medii-skandovali-lide-v-liberci-prisli-branit-nezavislost-ct-a-rozhlasu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/903966-ruce-pryc-od-medii-skandovali-lide-v-liberci-prisli-branit-nezavislost-ct-a-rozhlasu.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 13:35:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Richard Beneš</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Velké množství lidí s transparenty v rukou zaplnilo v sobotu po poledni náměstí v Liberci, aby vyjádřili podporu České televizi a ČRo. Reagovali tak na noční vyhrocené jednání Sněmovny, kdy vládní poslanci nečekaně prosadili v prvním čtení návrh novely, která ruší koncesionářské poplatky.</description></item><item><title>Běžkaři se těší: Sezona jim v Bedřichově v Jizerských horách začne nejspíš za měsíc</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903830-bezkarum-v-bedrichove-v-jizerskych-horach-zacne-sezona-nejspis-za-mesic.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903830-bezkarum-v-bedrichove-v-jizerskych-horach-zacne-sezona-nejspis-za-mesic.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Běžkařům v Bedřichově v Jizerských horách začne sezona nejspíš za měsíc. Obecně prospěšná společnost Jizerská začala tento týden s výrobou technického sněhu na stadionu, okruh na něm chce otevřít 21. listopadu.
